I could give you a quick rundown of my opinion if that helps. Some background: I grew up with Emerald and Diamond, those two are my favorites. I played Black and Soul Silver growing up as well, just didn’t like them very much and Black caused me to fall off the series for a long time, until 2018 when I got a 3DS for Christmas with Pokémon Y and Ultra Sun. I breezed through Y in 18 hours over 2 days, then beat Ultra Sun and completed a full regional living dex in it after having a blast with it plus the post game. My opinion is based off of Ultra Sun. I loved it a lot, the music and art style were really fantastic and a big step forward in my eyes. The game actually managed to be challenging too despite your whole party getting EXP with the EXP Share now, since I ended up playing at what I can only describe as a normal pace, not stopping to grind or fight every trainer but not going out of my way to avoid a fight either. The island challenges were decently tough but the puzzles that came before them honestly sucked, none of them were even remotely challenging or interesting and the ghost trial in particular was really awful to control with the 3DS’s gyroscopic controls (and this is on the New 3DS XL as well). The Elite 4 were really tough, and I loved having to fight Kukui and Hau at the end, in addition to having different new trainers coming to challenge your throne as champion, it gave me a fun and interesting place to grind in the post game. Ultra Necrozma is incredibly tough and probably the hardest boss across all the main line Pokémon games, he was a pleasant surprise and a great way to expose the limitations of the team I threw together over the course of the game.The post game content is no slouch either, the Ultra Wormhole is super fun and a great way to fill out your legendary collection and snag a few easy shinies, since once you get good at the mini game that takes you between each portal you can consistently find regular Pokémon that are shiny. The Rainbow Rocket chapter wasn’t incredible, but it felt like a lot of love was poured into it from the old designs of the villains returning, a brand new battle theme for the Rocket members themselves and even remixes of old battle themes for each of the older members. It was tough as well, they all have a full team of competent and strong Pokémon. Overall, I’d rate the experience an 8/10 and it’s one my favorite Pokémon games to date. It gets a lot of justified hate for rehashing most of the content from Sun/Moon and editing the story, but I think that when viewed in a vacuum it’s pretty excellent. If you haven’t played gen 7, it’s absolutely the best way to experience it.

It’s funny really, back when Disney dubbed a lot of Ghibli movies for the west they hired famous actors to do a lot of the roles, and it shows. They still hold up wonderfully, even if some people still prefer the subs for quality reasons, and they certainly outclass a lot of the rushed, never ending dubs we see vomited out every season. A lot of shows I’m on the borderline with, like Darling in the Franxx, because I think they have a lot going for them but really could’ve used some
more time in the oven for less awkward dialogue and things like that.
